title: BACE: Technical Skills & Applications - Technical Skills and Applications - Cloning & Recombinant DNA
subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: What is the primary function of a restriction enzyme (endonuclease)?
options: To cleave DNA at specific palindromic sequences.
To transport DNA into the cell.
questions.explain: Restriction enzymes recognize specific sequences (usually palindromes) and cut the phosphodiester backbone of DNA at those sites.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: In a plasmid vector, what is the function of the *ori* (origin of replication) sequence?
options: It allows the plasmid to replicate independently within the host bacterium.
It is the site where the gene of interest is inserted.
It produces the blue color in screening.
questions.explain: The *ori* sequence recruits the host cell's replication machinery, allowing the plasmid to replicate autonomously.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

The vector re-circularized without an insert.
The gene of interest was successfully inserted, disrupting the *lacZ* gene.
questions.explain: Successful insertion disrupts the *lacZ* $\alpha$-peptide gene. Functional *lacZ* turns X-gal blue. If disrupted (insert present), no functional $\beta$-galactosidase is made, resulting in white colonies.

questions.q: Which enzyme is used to covalently join the phosphate backbone of the insert and the vector?
questions.explain: DNA Ligase forms phosphodiester bonds between the 3'-OH and 5'-phosphate ends of DNA fragments.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: Why is Alkaline Phosphatase often treated onto a linearized plasmid vector before ligation?
options: To prevent the vector from self-ligating (re-circularizing).
questions.explain: Alkaline Phosphatase removes the 5' phosphate groups from the vector. Ligase requires a 5' phosphate to close the nick. This prevents the vector from closing on itself without an insert (which provides the phosphate).
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: What does 'transformation' refer to in the context of bacterial cloning?
options: The cutting of DNA by enzymes.
The uptake of foreign plasmid DNA by competent bacterial cells.
questions.explain: Transformation is the process by which competent bacterial cells take up naked DNA (plasmids) from the environment.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: Which feature of a plasmid allows for the selection of only those bacteria that have taken up the plasmid?
questions.explain: Bacteria without the plasmid die in the presence of the antibiotic. Only those with the plasmid (and the resistance gene) survive.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: Sticky ends generated by restriction enzymes are preferred over blunt ends for cloning because:
options: They can ligate to any other DNA fragment.
They provide complementary overhangs that facilitate correct annealing and directional efficiency.
They are more stable at high temperatures.
questions.explain: Sticky ends have complementary overhangs that transiently base-pair, stabilizing the interaction between insert and vector, making the ligation reaction much more efficient.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: To verify the orientation of an insert in a plasmid, which method is most effective?
options: Digest with restriction enzymes that cut asymmetrically within the insert and vector.
Run the plasmid on an SDS-PAGE gel.
questions.explain: Blue-White tells you if an insert is present, but not its orientation. Restriction digest mapping (or sequencing) is required to determine orientation based on expected fragment sizes.
questions.subject: Technical Skills and Applications

questions.q: What is the role of the promoter sequence located upstream of the Multiple Cloning Site (MCS) in an expression vector?
options: To initiate replication of the plasmid.
To drive the transcription of the inserted gene into mRNA.
To signal the end of translation.
questions.explain: In an expression vector, the promoter binds RNA polymerase to initiate transcription of the gene inserted into the MCS.
